answer: Each identity stakes 70 credit and posts a work claim on a public table frozen like a glacier. Each epoch a gale audit sweeps random rows and replays each claim; a hollow row—missing, copied, or key-mismatched—burns the 70 stake. The k-th fake costs 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 and lock 70,000, for a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 40 once and gets its 70 back; rented rows still carry the seller's key, so rented-table rings collapse.
